key_insight: Cubic HUBO captures substantial third-order configurational energy contributions that QUBO cannot represent in lithium-rich oxyfluorides.
engineering_relevance: Higher-order energy models could improve configurational modeling of disordered-rocksalt cathodes, provided magnetic-state dependence is accounted for.
method: Generate composition-preserving, fixed-geometry energy maps using spin-polarized DFT.
Compare quadratic QUBO and cubic HUBO fits for Li₂MnO₂F and Li₂Mn₀.₅Ti₀.₅O₂F.
Check third-order nonadditivity through direct DFT energy differences and compare magnetic initializations.
evidence_signal: Cubic HUBO substantially reduces fitting errors in both materials, while direct DFT differences confirm third-order nonadditivity and reveal strong electronic-state dependence in the Ti-containing material.
watch_item: Extracted higher-order terms are effective couplings among exchange variables, not uniquely identified microscopic three-atom interactions; magnetic-state consistency requires care.
paper_title: First-Principles Identification of Higher-Order Configurational Energy Terms and Their Magnetic-State Dependence in Lithium-Rich Oxyfluorides: From QUBO to HUBO
